examples.title: Complex amplitude
examples.question: For (1/√2)|0⟩ + (i/√2)|1⟩, find P(0) and P(1).
examples.answer: P(0)=50% and P(1)=50%. The state differs from |+⟩ by relative phase even though the computational-basis measurement is 50/50.

examples.title: Two Hadamards
examples.question: What happens when H is applied twice to |0⟩?
steps: H|+⟩ = |0⟩ because the |1⟩ amplitudes cancel and the |0⟩ amplitudes reinforce.
examples.answer: The state returns deterministically to |0⟩. This illustrates interference.

examples.title: Bell state
examples.question: What happens for |00⟩ → H on the first qubit → CNOT?
examples.answer: Measurement gives 00 or 11, each with probability 1/2; 01 and 10 do not occur for the ideal state.

examples.title: Normalization
examples.question: Why must |α|² + |β|² equal 1 for a normalized one-qubit state?
steps: The squared magnitudes are the probabilities of the two computational-basis measurement outcomes.
